title: Her rooms on G deck (the lower deck): R3, a sourced table of facts
written: 2026-11-20, by the R3 session (Claude Opus 5.5), under docs/research/RESEARCH_rooms_plans_licence_v1_1_2026-11-20.md, on the coordinator's word after the E-deck pilot
rules: Facts only: which room, where, how big, which door to which. No image or drawing of any plan is kept. Every row cites the reference read and the original checked, or says it was not checked. Bets are tagged as bets.
reference: ET: Encyclopedia Titanica's free deck plans, G deck (https://www.encyclopedia-titanica.org/titanic-deckplans/g-deck.html; drawn by Bruce Beveridge for Titanic The Ship Magnificent, The History Press 2008), read on the page in the built-in browser on 2026-11-20, nothing saved
original: Shipbuilder 1911: The Shipbuilder, Midsummer 1911 (the Olympic and Titanic number), plate 5, 'Lower Deck G' (with F, the orlops and the tank top), as reproduced by GG Archives (https://www.ggarchives.com/OT/Titanic/25-ImageLibrary/TheShipbuilder-10-Design-SpecialPlates.html); too small to read room by room.
how: As for E and F decks: walls by her frames, read off the frame numbers the reference prints every second frame along the centreline; the rest by eye, to about a frame and a foot (tag 'approx'). G deck's rows are coarser than E's and F's: blocks across her breadth where the reference draws rooms between passages, and one row a boiler room where G deck is no floor at all.

Frames to feet: the reference's own scale on this deck's image, 30.84 px a frame amidships (0.09735 ft a pixel), from the midship section between frames 1A and 1F. At that scale the plan's bulkheads C to L, N and O land within about 0.2 m of the model's.

y: feet from the centreline, port positive, at 0.0982 ft a pixel (F deck's breadth scale; this image's hull lines amidships are hidden by the bunkers' hatching). 'shell+' and 'shell-' are her side; in metres the tool puts it at the model's half-breadth halfway between G and F decks [stand-in for the reference's shell].

Between bulkheads E and K (frames 63F to 30A, the boiler rooms) G deck is not a floor: the reference draws the boiler casings and the tops of the coal bunkers, cross bunkers at each bulkhead and side bunkers outboard. Those rows are kind 'casing' or 'bunker', one a boiler room or cross bunker, across her breadth [read; the casings' own sides not read].
Doors: 2 ft 3 in by default [bet]. The reference marks no watertight door on G deck in the views read; the model has one at N ('G', 1).
Derived fields (x_m, y_m, poly_m, area_m2, zone, slab, plan_compartment) are written by: node tools/rooms_table.js --write data/rooms/G_deck.json

frames.note: Her frames as the reference draws them on G deck: [frame, feet forward of amidships]. Interpolated linearly between anchors. 'stern' is where her side meets the centreline on this deck.

bulkheads.note: Watertight bulkheads where the reference marks them on G deck (W.T.B. labels, written there as "A" to "P").
